content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic: ABIOC(KOI-011 Base64 Decode Of Agent Skill Prerequisite Block) FOLLOWED_BY ABIOC(KOI-011 Curl Pipe To Bash Dropper From Agent Lineage) FOLLOWED_BY BIOC(KOI-011 Dropped Shell Reads Multiple Developer Credential Files) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(KOI-011 Stolen Credentials Archived Into Staging Tarball) — all stitched by shared agent_hostname and actor_causality_id (CGO = the OpenClaw node agent runtime) so the prerequisite decode, the curl|bash dropper, the multi-credential read and the local loot staging collapse into ONE OpenClaw agentic-supply-chain incident. The chain closes on the endpoint: its terminal term is the loot-archive create, not the egress, so the rule fires in a lab with no authorised sink and no firewall in path.
rules.name: OpenClaw ClawHub Malicious Skill — Prerequisite Decode, curl|bash Dropper, Developer-Credential Read and Local Staging
